title: Unlocking Lossless Speedups in LLMs via Discrete Diffusion
content:
Subham Sekhar Sahoo,
    Lingjie Chen,
    Khiem Pham,
    Jonathan Geuter,
    Junlin Chen,
    Chaitanya Dwivedi,
    Varad Pimpalkhute,
    Yash Akhauri,
    Alexander Moreno,
    Mikhail Yurochkin,
    Zhenting Wang,
    Mostafa Elhoushi,
    Nolan Dey,
    Shane Bergsma,
    Joel Hestness,
    Hongyi Wang,
    John Thickstun,
    Eric Xing,
    Zhengzhong Liu
  
We introduce Uno, a diffusion-augmented LLM that
features two sets of weights:
- AR weights: Trained using next-token prediction loss to define an AR distribution.
- Diffusion weights: Trained to generate multiple tokens in parallel from the AR distribution.
To sample from Uno, we propose 
- Unlike speculative decoding methods, Uno does not require a separately trained draft model and achieves higher throughput across all batch sizes.
- Unlike self-speculative deciding approaches, Uno is lossless.
In this repo, we release the code for:
- 
Inference
  - A Nano-vLLM-based inference engine for $\Psi$ -Spec sampler.
    - 
Linear Sampler for high system throughput.
    - 
Tree sampler for high per-request throughput.
  - 
  - Ready-to-run recipes for Uno Qwen3 8B, Uno 8B, and Uno 1B.
- A Nano-vLLM-based inference engine for 
- 
Training
  - A conditional-LoRA diffusion training pipeline for Uno Qwen3 8B.
  - OpenThoughts data preparation and progressive block-size curricula.
  - Multi-node Slurm launchers with checkpoint resume support.
- 
Evaluation
  - One shared generation and scoring pipeline across model families.
  - Benchmark-specific data loaders and graders.
  - Accuracy, tokens per forward (TPF), and tokens per second (TPS) metrics.
  - Single-benchmark, full-suite, and persistent pull-based launchers.
The repository is organized around the workflows users run:
- nano_vllm_uno/ : Inference engine optimized for Uno, with
model execution, KV-cache management, and lossless linear and tree sampling.
- generation.py : Shared model loading, conditional-LoRA
attachment, prompt formatting, generation, and TPF/TPS accounting.
- inference.py : Free-form prompt inference with linear or
tree sampling.
- evaluation/ : Benchmark protocols, dataset loaders,
generation, parsers, and benchmark-specific graders.
- training/ : Data preparation, conditional-LoRA training,
diffusion objectives, curricula, and checkpointing.
- examples/ : Model-specific training, inference, and evaluation
recipes that call the shared workflows.
Create a Python 3.10 environment and install Uno with its evaluation and training dependencies:
conda create -n nano-vllm-uno python=3.10 pip -y
conda activate nano-vllm-uno
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
python -m pip install torch==2.11.0 \
  --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128
python -m pip install \
  'https://github.com/lesj0610/flash-attention/releases/download/v2.8.3-cu12-torch2.11/flash_attn-2.8.3%2Bcu12torch2.11cxx11abiTRUE-cp310-cp310-linux_x86_64.whl'
python -m pip install -e '.[eval,train]'
This installs FlashAttention-2 (FA2), which is sufficient for linear decoding. Tree verification additionally requires FlashAttention-3 (FA3):
python -m pip install ninja==1.13.0
git clone --depth 1 --branch v2.8.3 \
  https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention.git
cd flash-attention/hopper
MAX_JOBS=16 python -m pip install --no-build-isolation .
Public checkpoints can be downloaded without a Hugging Face token. A token is still required for gated datasets such as GPQA and for any private or gated model repository.
All public model recipes live under examples/. Each recipe supplies the
model-specific defaults and delegates to the same shared training, inference,
or evaluation workflow.
To train Uno Qwen3 8B, prepare the training data and run the shared training entry point as follows.
Prepare the pinned OpenThoughts3-1.2M corpus once in shared storage:
python -m training.prepare_openthoughts \
  --output /path/to/openthoughts-uno-4095 \
  --cache-dir /path/to/hf-cache \
  --num-proc 32
The following is a single-GPU command. Gradient accumulation preserves the released global batch size of 128:
python -m training.train \
  --dataset-path /path/to/openthoughts-uno-4095 \
  --output-dir /path/to/uno-training \
  --curriculum training/configs/uno_3epoch_curriculum.yaml \
  --deepspeed training/configs/deepspeed_zero2.json \
  --per-device-batch-size 8 \
  --gradient-accumulation-steps 16 \
  --learning-rate 1e-5 \
  --warmup-steps 562 \
  --lora-target all \
  --lora-rank 128 \
  --lora-alpha 2048 \
  --ce-alpha 0 \
  --kl-beta 0 \
  --tv-gamma 1
See training/train.py and
training/configs/uno_3epoch_curriculum.yaml
for the complete training configuration. Resume an interrupted run with
--resume-from-checkpoint /path/to/checkpoint and the same --output-dir.
Use the model recipe that matches the checkpoint. All three recipes call the
same shared inference.py workflow:
# Uno Qwen3 8B
bash examples/uno_qwen3_8B/run_inference.sh \
  --prompt "Solve 2 + 2 and explain your reasoning."
# Uno 8B
bash examples/uno_8B/run_inference.sh \
  --prompt "Solve 2 + 2 and explain your reasoning."
# Uno 1B
bash examples/uno_1B/run_inference.sh \
  --prompt "Solve 2 + 2 and explain your reasoning."
The example launchers use linear sampling by default. To enable tree sampling, install FA3 and pass the tree parameters to the same entry point:
ATTENTION_BACKEND=fa3 \
  bash examples/uno_qwen3_8B/run_inference.sh \
    --prompt "Solve 2 + 2 and explain your reasoning." \
    --diffusion-block-size 16 \
    --tree-candidate-top-k 32 \
    --tree-verify-size 60
The command prints generated text together with output-token count, elapsed
time, TPS, decoder statistics, and TPF. Common controls include
--temperature, --top-p, --top-k, --max-tokens,
--diffusion-block-size, and --max-num-seqs.
The evaluation workflow uses canonical benchmark settings from
evaluation/benchmarks.py. Generation and grading are separate internally,
while each model recipe runs both stages through one command. Evaluation
results are provided in each model-specific subdirectory under
examples/.
Missing public datasets are prepared automatically. They can also be prepared in advance:
export UNO_EVAL_DATA_DIR=/path/to/uno-eval-data
python -m evaluation.prepare_data \
  --output-dir "${UNO_EVAL_DATA_DIR}"
Keep UNO_EVAL_DATA_DIR set when running run_eval.sh. The evaluation runner
will reuse the prepared JSONL files from this directory and will prepare any
missing benchmark there automatically.
Set the shared output and parallelism options, then choose the model recipe:
export RESULTS_ROOT=/path/to/results
export DATA_PARALLEL_SIZE=1
# Uno Qwen3 8B
bash examples/uno_qwen3_8B/run_eval.sh gsm8k
# Uno 8B
bash examples/uno_8B/run_eval.sh gsm8k
# Uno 1B
bash examples/uno_1B/run_eval.sh gsm8k
Supported benchmarks:
- Math: aime24 ,aime25 ,aime26 ,gsm8k , andmath500 .
- Knowledge: arc_challenge ,gpqa_diamond ,hle , andomniscience .
- Code: humaneval andmbpp .
- Instruction and long-context reasoning:
ifeval andlcr .
Run the complete suite sequentially:
MODEL_EXAMPLE=uno_qwen3_8B \
RESULTS_ROOT=/path/to/results \
DATA_PARALLEL_SIZE=1 \
  bash evaluation/run_suite.sh
Set MODEL_EXAMPLE to uno_qwen3_8B, uno_8B, or uno_1B.
Uno's runtime builds on Nano-vLLM, and its training utilities are adapted from LlamaFactory. See NOTICE for attribution and license notices.

}

report.summary: Uno open-sources diffusion-augmented LLMs that decode multiple tokens in parallel, achieving lossless speedups without draft models.
report.background: Autoregressive LLMs generate one token per forward pass, so output speed is bound by step count and memory bandwidth. Speculative decoding and self-speculative variants use a separate draft model or early-exit heads to propose blocks, then verify with the target model, introducing acceptance/rejection overhead and possible distribution shifts. Uno takes a different route: discrete diffusion is added as a second set of weights that learns the target AR distribution and proposes/refines entire blocks in parallel. Because verification is based on the original AR distribution, output is lossless. The code release includes a Nano-vLLM runtime for linear/tree sampling, conditional-LoRA diffusion training over OpenThoughts3, recipes for 1B/8B/Qwen3-8B, and an evaluation suite.
key_points: Hybrid AR+diffusion weights: Uno keeps standard autoregressive next-token weights and adds auxiliary diffusion weights trained with discrete-diffusion objectives to model the AR distribution. Training uses conditional LoRA, a progressive block-size curriculum, and OpenThoughts3 data, enabling the model to form multiple tokens per step rather than one at a time.

No separate draft model: unlike speculative decoding, Uno does not require a small sampled draft model or extra acceptance heads. Its diffusion weights propose token blocks, and the paper reports higher throughput than speculative decoding at all batch sizes. This makes the speedup lossless and removes draft-model tuning from the deployment workflow.

Two decoding modes: the released inference engine supports a linear sampler that prioritizes system throughput and a tree sampler that maximizes per-request throughput by verifying multiple candidate continuations in parallel. Tree verification uses FlashAttention-3, while linear decoding works with FlashAttention-2; users can tune block size, temperature, top-p/top-k, and max tokens.

Open, reproducible implementation: the repo includes model execution, KV-cache management, shared data preparation, training and evaluation launchers, Slurm scripts, checkpoint resume support, and runnable recipes for Uno Qwen3 8B, Uno 8B, and Uno 1B. Public checkpoints are available, and evaluations cover math, knowledge, code, instruction following, and long-context reasoning benchmarks.
report.impact: Uno shows that discrete diffusion can be attached to standard AR LLMs as a practical, lossless inference accelerator rather than as a separate generation paradigm. For AI developers, the absence of a separately trained draft model simplifies serving stacks and avoids the fragile draft-target gaps seen in speculative decoding. Production systems may benefit from higher tokens-per-second and throughput, lowering latency and cost per generation. The open-source code, public checkpoints, and ready-to-run recipes also lower the barrier for researchers to experiment with diffusion-augmented inference and compare metrics such as tokens-per-forward and accuracy across standard benchmarks.
report.tools: Follow the official ifm-ai/uno repository and reproduce inference with its example launchers, e.g. examples/uno_qwen3_8B/run_inference.sh. For tree sampling, install FlashAttention-3 and pass --tree-candidate-top-k and --tree-verify-size. Use the shared training/train.py pipeline to run conditional-LoRA diffusion training, and the evaluation/run_suite.sh script to check GSM8K, AIME, GPQA, MBPP, and IFEval results. Related projects worth watching include Nano-vLLM and LLaMA-Factory, which Uno builds on.
